title.value: Boosting Latent Diffusion with Perceptual Objectives
title.justification: The title is provided at the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: Boosting Latent Diffusion with Perceptual Objectives

analysis.description: The paper proposes a novel approach to improve the quality of images generated by Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) for high-resolution generative image tasks by introducing a latent perceptual loss (LPL). This loss utilizes the internal features of autoencoder decoders to enhance image sharpness and realism, addressing the disconnect between diffusion models and autoencoder decoders. The approach is validated on various datasets, showing significant improvements in image generation metrics.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments using various datasets and models to validate the effectiveness of the proposed latent perceptual loss (LPL).
type.quote: Extensive experiments with models trained on three datasets at 256 and 512 resolution show improved quantitative – with boosts between 6% and 20% in FID – and qualitative results when using our perceptual loss.

name.justification: The paper's main contribution is towards generating high-quality images using latent diffusion.
name.quote: LDMs learn the data distribution in the latent space of an autoencoder and produce images by mapping the generated latents into RGB image space using the AE decoder.
